findings.title: Prepared/applied rows are not bound to the same proposal
findings.evidence: The loop validates fourteen typed fields separately, raw previous_sha256 and consecutive numbers/parity. It does not compare paired prepared/applied documents after excluding only generation/state. A byte-valid applied envelope can name a different transaction, candidate, semantics or source/request while retaining a valid raw predecessor link.
findings.effect: Retained journal copy/type/hash-chain evidence is weaker than full production proposal continuity. This is a validation coverage gap, not an observed native failure or a demonstrated signature blocker.
findings.next_action: Preserve V1 and add a fixed successor that compares every retained prepared/applied proposal field except generation/state.

findings.title: New proposal identity and final physical CFG are not linked
findings.evidence: For retained four records, a later prepared record is not required to have a transaction different from the preceding applied record, as production _chain requires. The last applied.candidate_sha256 is not compared with physical retained cfg.sha256. strict_journal checks individual types/hashes but not these associations.
findings.effect: The copied CFG and individually valid retained journal chain can be mutually inconsistent without these predicates rejecting them. Physical source stability after capture does not add the missing cross-file binding.
findings.next_action: Successor should compare new-operation transaction identity and bind final applied candidate SHA to copied actual CFG SHA. Do not add a cross-operation prepared.original_sha256 == prior applied.candidate_sha256 requirement: production does not enforce it and legitimate prior CFG changes must not be falsely refused.
